minimum-spec: extra keys carry no shared meaning (SPEC section 2)
host-owned acknowledged key: presence is never a spec violation

the engine's local/ contract: a dir without pack.json is a loose WIP dir and skips quietly (pinned by their packs.test.js); the linter refuses at author time because a PUBLIC pack without a manifest is never legitimate - the WIP-friendliness belongs to local/, visibility is theirs
visibility dirs are optional roots to the engine (public/ or local/); SPEC section 1 makes the public directory contract required - the linter enforces the spec at author time

the one true enforcement gap on record: the engine keys the shared seen map by manifest.name and never compares to the directory; the 8/8 dir match was the #19 data-level invariant. The linter enforces the SPEC norm (section 2: mismatch = load refuse); engine parity is the engine-first question, crosslinked in the SPEC receipts to crashtest#19/#25

tally.reading: Every divergence row is a PACK-STRUCT STRICTNESS the engine does not share (author-time authoring gates vs load-time reality), except armedByKey-non-string which is the SPEC's string-type rule. No divergence is a spec violation on either side - which is exactly what this matrix exists to prove.
